profile.name: Gainjeonmokdan
profile.tagline: A 19th-century Korean court dance where dancers circle a vase of peonies.
profile.insight: Initiated by Crown Prince Hyomyeong in 1829 to please his father, dancers delicately pluck peonies from a central vase in calm, measured movements.
profile.profile: Gainjeonmokdan is a traditional Korean court dance, known as a jeongjae, which translates literally to "beautiful people plucking peonies." Initiated and arranged by Crown Prince Hyomyeong in 1829, the dance was created to please his father, King Sunjo, and was first recorded in the Mujajinjak uiqwe in 1828. During a performance, a large vase of peonies is placed center stage while female dancers divided into two groups move around it. The dancers pick a peony one by one and perform in a calm movement accompanied by vocal verses known as Changsa.
profile.profile_long:
Gainjeonmokdan is a historical Korean court dance, classified under the genre of jeongjae. The title translates literally to "beautiful people plucking peonies." The dance was initiated and arranged by Hyomyeong Seja, also known as Crown Prince Hyomyeong, in 1829 as a filial offering to please his father, King Sunjo. Early documentation of the performance appears in the historical text Mujajinjak uiqwe, published in 1828. 

Performance staging centers around a large vase filled with peonies placed directly in the center of the stage. Female dancers are split into two groups that navigate around the central vase, anticipating the flowers before individually picking a peony. Following this gesture, the performers execute a calm sequence of movements. The performance is accompanied by Changsa, which consist of the verses of the accompanying song used for the dance and other traditional performing arts.

claims.text: Gainjeonmokdan is a Korean court dance called jeongjae, meaning beautiful people plucking peonies.
claims.quote: Gainjeonmokdan (Korean pronunciation: [ka.in dʑʌmoktan]) is a Korean court dance (called jeongjae 정재 in Korean), and literally means "beautiful people plucking peonies".

claims.text: It was initiated and arranged by Crown Prince Hyomyeong in 1829 to please King Sunjo and was first recorded in the Mujajinjak uiqwe in 1828.
claims.quote: initiated and arranged by Hyomyeong Seja (Crown Prince Hyomyeong) in 1829 to please his father, King Sunjo. Gainjeonmokdan was first recorded in Mujajinjak uiqwe (무자진작의궤) in 1828.

claims.text: Peonies in a large vase are placed in the center of the stage while female dancers from two groups move around it, pick a peony one by one, and dance in a calm movement.
claims.quote: peonies in a large vase for a prop are placed in the center of the stage, and then female dancers from divided two groups anticipate the flowers as moving around the vase. Dancers pick a peony one by one, and then dance in a calm movement.
